note: Authored tuning. A rough one-room log cabin takes about 15 worker-days: in November 1846 the Graves cabin at Truckee Lake went up in about three days with Eddy's help (Donner Party Diary, November 1846). Each fit, willing adult gives one worker-day per building day; Carpentry works half again as fast. A hatchet (the period's axe) is needed. A finished cabin keeps out cold exposure and storms and cuts winter illness; it does nothing for hunger, scurvy or animals without grass.

settle.note: Spencer: a party may settle anywhere at any time, within the constraints. Missouri and the edge of the Willamette settlements are open to settlers. At a trading post the party stays on as hands or squatters, unless the post refuses it over known crimes. Everywhere else is Native country: the people there decide, once per party and place, and refuse squatters more often than not; a party they have heard ill of is refused. Peoples per stop are approximate for 1848 and only name who the party would have to ask.
